$description: Data-driven report configuration consumed by scripts/report.py.
Every value the report uses to classify, threshold, or label content lives here so
tuning a benchmark does not require code changes. Sections:
- project:               human-facing project metadata + default workload label
- target_registry:       device pattern -> rated specs (BF16, BW, capacity)
- thresholds:            numeric pass/fail / classification thresholds
- pdf_reference_targets: source-pilot per-scope MFU targets (% of measured peak)
- status_pills:          status string -> CSS class for the HTML pill renderer
- status_severity:       overall verdict logic (FAIL > WARN > SKIP > PASS)
- glossary:              acronyms used throughout the report
Override at runtime with: scripts/report.py --report-config <path>
Per-op meas/theory bands (TESTPLAN §10.4):
<=at_hardware_limit         -> kernel at hardware ceiling
(at_hw, tunable]            -> tuning win available
>tunable                    -> implementation-quality issue (P4 candidate)
Calibration-drift gate (config-shape sanity, blocks reproduction sign-off).
MFU vs PDF tolerance (per scope) sets the SC-4 acceptable band.
Sweep peak fractions classify the GEMM size sweep transition curve.
Fragmentation warning ratio fires the chunked-vs-contig insight.
Generic fallback for source-pilot per-scope MFU targets on the
measured-peak basis. The PRIMARY home for these is each workload
config's `source_pilot_reference.pdf_reference_targets_pct` block
(see configs/escher_14b_480p.json) so they live next to the other
workload-specific reference numbers (reference_totals_per_block,
peak_tflops, ici_ring_gb_s). The report only falls back to these
values when neither the workload config nor mfu.json supplies them.

status_pills.$description: Status string -> CSS class. Falls back to 'pill-skip' for unknown statuses.

status_severity.$description: Verdict-aggregation order; status with the highest severity wins.

glossary.definition: Arithmetic Intensity — FLOPs per byte of memory traffic.
All-Gather (collective; concatenates rank-local tensors across all ranks).
Fused All-Gather + Matmul kernel — overlaps the collective with the GEMM.
All-to-All (collective; alternative TP topology to AG+RS).
Brain Floating-Point 16-bit — 1 sign / 8 exponent / 7 mantissa.
Double Data Rate (system DRAM, used on CPU hosts as the memory roof).
Diffusion Transformer — the workload family being benchmarked.
End-to-End — wall-clock-timed full forward pass; contrasts with sum-of-ops.
Feed-Forward Network (the two-linear MLP block inside each transformer layer).
General Matrix-Multiply (the dominant compute kernel in transformer stacks).
High-Bandwidth Memory (the on-package DRAM on AMD Instinct GPUs).
Model FLOPs Utilization — observed throughput / peak throughput, on a chosen basis.
Fused Matmul + Reduce-Scatter kernel — overlaps the GEMM with the collective.
NVIDIA Communication Collectives Library — collective-comm backend on NVIDIA GPUs.
ROCm Communication Collectives Library — RCCL is to ROCm what NCCL is to CUDA.
AMD's open-source HPC/AI compute stack (the platform layer below PyTorch on AMD).
Reduce-Scatter (collective; reduces and partitions across all ranks).
ROCm Validation Suite — `rvs gst` is the canonical BF16 compute peak ground truth.
Success-Criterion N from TESTPLAN §1.2 — the benchmark's pass/fail grid.
Scaled Dot-Product Attention — torch's attention API (default vs flash backends).
Tera (10¹²) Floating-Point Operations Per Second.
Tensor-Parallel — the multi-GPU layout for the transformer stack.
Variational Auto-Encoder — out of scope (only the transformer stack is profiled).
